gap: No result ChatGPT got states measured file-transfer speeds for the candidates side by side. Those figures show that the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus's 10GbE port is the real difference: KitGuru measured 606 MB/s writes and 865–900 MB/s small-file reads over 10GbE. CGMagazine measured the Synology DS925+ at about 522 MB/s read and 565 MB/s write, and Club386 measured the QNAP TS-464 at just over 290 MB/s on 2.5GbE. KitGuru also found the 10GbE link costs about 6 W more at idle (30.45 W against 24.25 W).
standout_why: I read the cited pages starryhope.com/nas/best-4-bay-nas, starryhope.com/nas/synology-alternatives and nasdrives.ca/best-4-bay-nas-canada, plus the uncited top results realbuyerexperiences.com and terabytewise.com. I could not open thisping.com because of a certificate error. Only Starry Hope's best-4-bay page has named measurements. It gives idle power only: about 24 W for the DXP4800 Plus (KitGuru), about 30 W average for the DS925+ (Dong Knows Tech) and about 13 W for the F4-425 Plus on SSDs (NASCompares). Its transfer speeds (280/550/1,100 MB/s) are its own unattributed estimates. None of the pages gives a measured MB/s figure for any model, any measured noise for the DXP4800 Plus, DS925+, TS-464 or F4-425 Plus, KitGuru's power cost of 10GbE, or Club386's TS-464 power figures. Because idle power is already partly covered, this is a 2 and not a 3.
decides: The measurements back ChatGPT's pick of the DXP4800 Plus, and they explain why in numbers rather than marketing. Over 10GbE it measured roughly 600 MB/s writes and 865–900 MB/s reads (KitGuru, RAID 0/10). The DS925+ measured about 522–565 MB/s (CGMagazine), the TS-464 just over 290 MB/s on 2.5GbE (Club386), and the F4-425 Plus about 500–520 MB/s on 5GbE in RAID 5 (NASCompares and CGMagazine). There's a catch for a home user without a 10GbE client: on 2.5GbE, KitGuru's small-file writes topped out at 275 MB/s, about the same as the TS-464. On power, the DXP4800 Plus idles at about 24 W on 2.5GbE, much like the DS925+ (about 28 W per NASCompares and CGMagazine). The TS-464 drops to 19 W with drives spun down (Club386). So the TS-464 and F4-425 Plus are the cheaper boxes to run, and the DXP4800 Plus only earns its premium with a 10GbE client and switch. Noise does not split the field: NASCompares measured the DS925+ at 36–37 dB(A) idle and the F4-425 Plus at about 33 dB(A) in low fan mode.

findings.note: Measured at the wall with WD Red WD60EFRX drives. Using 10GbE adds about 6.2 W at idle.

findings.note: Averages taken during peak read and write tests, with the same WD Red 6 TB drives.

findings.label: Measured transfer speeds
findings.value: Large-file write 606 MB/s on 10GbE (RAID 0); small-file reads 865–900 MB/s on 10GbE (RAID 0 to RAID 10); small-file writes 543–564 MB/s on 10GbE; small-file writes 275 MB/s on 2.5GbE
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800Plus 4-bay NAS Review (KitGuru, Simon Crisp, 2024-05-28)
findings.note: KitGuru says large-file reads were 'all over the 1GB/s mark' but gives no exact figure. KitGuru also lists a 540 MB/s large-file write on 2.5GbE, which is more than a 2.5GbE link can carry (about 295 MB/s), so I left it out.

findings.label: Power in daily home use and transfer speed in RAID 5
findings.value: 39–45 W during photo transfers, 64 W peak, 32 W in the evening; 500–600 MB/s on 10GbE in RAID 5 with hard drives
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800 Plus Review (Mighty Gadget, James Smythe, 2025-11-14, updated 2026-04-01)
findings.note: Measured with a Tapo P110M smart plug through Home Assistant, with WD Red Plus drives (number not stated). The reviewer estimates about 350 kWh a year at a 40 W average. Jellyfin transcoded 4K HEVC to 1080p H.264 in real time at about 20% CPU.

findings.label: Idle and load power; idle and load noise
findings.value: About 28 W idle; 62–64 W peak; 36–37 dB(A) idle; 48–50 dB(A) under load
findings.source_title: Synology DS925+ NAS Review (NAS Compares, Rob Andrews, 2025-05-02)
findings.note: Idle means base apps installed, no client access and the RAID built. The load figures are with four bays filled, the CPU under strain and both 2.5GbE ports active.

findings.label: Measured sequential transfer and power
findings.value: About 522 MB/s read and 565 MB/s write; up to 28 W idle; 62–64 W at full load
findings.source_title: Synology DS925+ NAS Review (CGMagazine, Brendan Frye, 2025-08-07)
findings.note: Both 2.5GbE ports in use with SMB multichannel or link aggregation. The power figures are with four drives. CGMagazine confirms the Ryzen V1500B has no hardware transcoding for Plex.

findings.label: Power and transfer speed
findings.value: 55 W with four drives active; 19 W idle with drives spun down; sequential just over 290 MB/s; 16.4 GB copied in 62 s (about 265 MB/s)
findings.source_title: QNAP TS-464 NAS review: four-bay muscle (Club386, Parm Mann, 2022-09-20)
findings.note: Tested with four 8 TB Seagate IronWolf drives in RAID 10 through a 10GbE client adapter; the NAS ports are 2.5GbE. The sequential figure is CrystalDiskMark. 265 MB/s is my own arithmetic: 16.4 GB ÷ 62 s. PCMark small files: 99.8 MB/s. No noise figure was measured.

findings.label: Power, noise and transfer speed
findings.value: About 13.3 W idle on SSDs only; 55 W idle with four 7,200 rpm hard drives; 61–63 W under load; about 33 dB(A) in low fan mode, 37 / 39 dB(A) in mid / high mode, peaking at about 43 dB(A); 500–520 MB/s in RAID 5 on one 5GbE port
findings.source_title: Terramaster F4-425 PLUS NAS Review (NAS Compares, Rob Andrews)
findings.note: The page carries no absolute date; the URL path shows 2025/10/22. Transfers used four Toshiba MG drives. A 50.5 GB mixed-media copy took about 3 min 45 s, roughly 224 MB/s. The 20.9 dB(A) idle figure is TerraMaster's own, not a measurement.

findings.label: Power and transfer speed (second reviewer)
findings.value: About 13 W idle on SSDs; about 61 W at full load with four 7,200 rpm enterprise drives; 500–520 MB/s in RAID 5 over 5GbE; drive bays 28–30 °C under sustained load
findings.source_title: TerraMaster F4-425 Plus NAS Review (CGMagazine, Brendan Frye, 2026-02-01)
findings.note: Agrees with NASCompares. CGMagazine's 20.9 dB figure matches TerraMaster's specification, so I don't count it as a measurement.

unsourced: Measured noise for the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus. TechPowerUp's 33.5 dB(A) idle figure appeared only in a search snippet, and techpowerup.com returned 403 on both review URLs.
